page: Amazon Web Services m9g.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton Gen9 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 4 dedicated physical cores with 4 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 model. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and does not include local storage or a GPU.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.5 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.09 GB/sec, and Geekbench single-core testing with a score of 2337.0. Memory performance is also highly rated, with a top-tier PassMark memory score and a cached read-only small block memory bandwidth of 527.19 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance and complex instruction sets show some limitations. The PassMark CPU score falls into the bottom 25%, and the instance exhibits poor performance in prompt processing for medium-sized 7B LLM models, registering 11.27 tokens/sec.

Given its dedicated ARMv9 cores and balanced 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the m9g.xlarge offers a resource-dense profile for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight database operations, as demonstrated by its average performance in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. It is less suitable for workloads requiring heavy multi-threaded execution, complex extended CPU instructions, or large-scale LLM inference.

It features 4 dedicated physical cores with 4 vCPUs, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, running on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core performance, particularly in single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, text processing, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from strong single-core execution and high memory bandwidth, while avoiding heavy multi-threaded or complex instruction-set tasks.
